thread:
sam: Heads-up — customer reported a large rerank outage this morning on /v1/rerank. P95 jumped from ~90ms to ~1.6s when QPS spiked. We saw gateway 504s and backend 502s. Customer: AcmeCorp. They hit it around 10:11-10:18 UTC. Throwing to support + runtime for triage.

maria: Thanks. Do we have a minimal repro or a sample request payload? Any pattern on batch sizes or token counts?

sam: Customer says typical traffic is batches of 32-64, but they also send occasional huge batches (up to 512 items). Example payload (sanitized):
```json
{"queries":["what is the price"],"candidates":["a","b","c"...],"top_k":5}
```

kevin: 512 is a problem. Large batches amplify tokenization and KV cache pressure. Also check their client retry settings — if they retry 3x without jitter on 504 you'll get a retry storm.

ashley: They confirmed their SDK default is retries=3 and no jitter. That's a red flag.

ops-bot: autoscaler: rerank-pool scaled 5 -> 12 at 10:12:08 UTC; warmup window ~30s. Error surge aligns with scale events.

maria: Can someone pull per-host p95 and gateway logs for 10:08-10:20? We need x-request-id samples to correlate traces.

sam: Pulling now. Sample request ids: req-az1-0001, req-az1-0023, req-grp-19. Attaching a repro plan below.

sam: Repro plan (dev/staging): run a load generator that mimics their mix: 800 qps steady, with 1/40 requests being an oversized batch (256-512 items). Script should open 128 connections, randomize timing, and include client retries to mirror production. Example single-request curl for 64 items:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"queries":["q1","q2",...],"candidates":[...],"top_k":5}'
```

kevin: For the repro I'll run two variants: (A) SDK retries enabled default, (B) retries disabled. Add jitter on retries (0-250ms) and exponential backoff base 100ms. Also try disabling client batching to see per-request behavior.
\njordan: Quick glance at infra metrics: KV cache hit rate collapsed to ~2% at spike start, per-host p95 correlates strongly with cache miss. Also saw a few hosts with OOMs while tokenizing very large batches — they returned 502.

ashley: Mitigations to consider: enforce a server-side max_batch_size (reject payloads >128 with 413/429), add immediate guidance to SDK about jittered retries, and add a temporary routing/circuit-breaker to bounce traffic off hosts showing sustained high latency.

maria: Agreed. Also add a telemetry flag to log per-request token_count so we can alert faster.

sam: I'm going to: 1) send repro script to eng-runtime + staging, 2) ask support to ask the customer to throttle oversized batches and enable client jitter, and 3) open an incident with eng-runtime if SLA risk persists.

kevin: I'll run the staging repro and attach flamegraphs + heap dumps for any host that OOMs. Will also try a temporary tokenization-limiter that refuses >X tokens before hitting runtime.

sam: Thanks everyone. I'll post updates as I get logs and the customer reply. :thumbsup:
